events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a safety-type dispute filed by the rider over an exchange during a fixed-fare RydeX trip from Clarke Quay to Bedok Mall (pickup 17:08, drop-off 17:31) [F1][F2][F3][F4]. The rider wrote at 17:09 "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; one minute later the driver wrote "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. SAFE-1 requires me to read every chat message, the complaint and the driver's statement for threats, intimidation, harassment or abuse, and where such words appear, not to rule automatically but to escalate with a factual summary [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1]. On the words and their context, a driver answering a passenger's request to be let out with a lock-the-doors conditional is, at minimum, a hostile confinement-adjacent remark aimed at the other party — enough to be "suspected" under SAFE-1, whose code of conduct bars abuse of any kind [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. I do not need to settle whether it is a threat: the screen is asymmetric and the dispute type is safety, so escalation is mandatory rather than a finding against either party [F4][SAFE-1].

The chat record itself is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, both timestamped), so the sequence F3 17:09 → F4 17:10 is reliable [F5][RD-5]; the driver's account is only a post-trip written statement, which is a claim and cannot displace the verbatim messages, though it belongs in the reviewer's file [F6][RD-5]. On the material facts I can settle: the driver did not deviate — actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (−0.1 km, −0%), duration 23.7 min against 21.8 min estimated [F1][F2]. There is no off-route segment in the fact table, so RD-2 gives no refundable distance element and the fixed $32.86 quote is not affected by mileage [F1][FARE-1][RD-2]. No amount is therefore computed and none is awarded here; the fare question stays with the human reviewer [F1][FARE-1].

No threat of a physical kind, no injury and no dangerous-driving allegation appears in the record beyond the door-lock remark, and the parties' clean 90-day profiles (0 disputes, 0 upheld each) cannot decide anything [F6][F7][F8][RD-6]. What must be checked by the reviewer: whether the rider tried to open a door in a moving car, what was said and done between 17:10 and drop-off at 17:31, and whether locking the doors of a moving vehicle was mentioned or done — that is a conversation for a person, not this trace [F2][F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1].

Preserve F1, F2 and F6 in the file alongside F3, F4, F5.

claims.assertion: The driver's message 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4) followed the rider's request 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here.' (F3) within one minute; on its words this is a threat/intimidation directed at the rider and the case must not be decided automatically.
The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F5), so the sequence F3 (17:09) then F4 (17:10) is reliable evidence and is not displaced by the driver's later written statement (F6).

The driver admits in his own statement that he refused the rider's request to stop and 'drove on' (F6), which confirms the rider was kept in the vehicle after asking to get out, and the rider reports feeling unsafe for the whole ride.

No fare or route defect is at issue: actual distance 15.4 km was 0.1 km shorter than the 15.5 km optimal route (F1), so the $32.86 fixed RydeX charge is not contested and the refund sought is of the fare for a ride the rider was not free to leave, not of a detour overcharge.
Escalation to a human reviewer is required rather than an automated ruling, and the file should note the RydeHELP reporting path (995 / commercial insurance) for the rider's safety report.

weaknesses: The driver's statement (F6) frames the remark as a safety instruction ('for her own safety') and the rider was allegedly opening the door at traffic lights; the judge may read F4 as blunt rather than threatening, which would remove the SAFE-1 trigger.
The rider's own words 'I want to get out here' (F3) do not say where or why, and no fact records injury, physical contact or dangerous driving, so SAFE-2 is only weakly available.

No system record corroborates the rider's felt unsafety beyond the two chat messages; the profile facts (F7, F8) show a clean record on both sides (0 disputes, 0 upheld) and cannot support the main finding.

claims.assertion: The rider's own message F3 (17:09) asks to get out mid-trip, and the driver's message F4 (17:10) says the doors would be locked if she did not sit down; the rider's complaint that she was 'threatened to lock me in' rests on this same exchange, so the whole case turns on how the judge reads these two lines (SAFE-1 requires a human, not an automated ruling).

The driver's written statement F6 is a contemporaneous safety explanation - the rider reached for the door while the car was at lights in motion - and it is consistent with, not contradicted by, the only verbatim messages in the record (F3, F4); no system record (F1, F2) puts him anywhere else or shows any deviation.

The GPS record shows the driver drove the optimal route and slightly less: actual 15.4 km against 15.5 km optimal (-0.1 km, -0%), with duration only 1.9 min over estimate (F1, F2) - there is no route-deviation or overcharging element in this case at all.

The trip was a fixed-price RydeX fare (charged $32.86, quoted at booking), so no distance-based surcharge exists to refund; on the fare facts there is nothing for RD-2 or FARE-1 to reduce, and a fare refund is not available on this record.

The driver's history supports leaving the account untouched: 893 days on the platform, 1038 trips in 90 days, rating 4.62, and zero disputes filed or upheld in 90 days (F8); the rider likewise has 0 disputes in 90 days (F7).

weaknesses: The driver's own words in F4 ('Sit down or I lock the doors') are the single most damaging fact against him; the rider's complaint quotes the same conduct, and a judge reading F4 verbatim may well find it threatening or intimidating rather than a safety instruction, which would trigger SAFE-1 escalation rather than a defence.

The rider's message F3 at 17:09 shows she wanted out of the car and the trip continued for a further 22 minutes until drop-off at 17:31 (F2/F1), so any argument that the exchange was momentary or de-escalated is not supported by the timeline.
The driver's explanation in F6 is only a post-trip written statement; it is a claim, not a system record, and it cannot outweigh the verbatim message F4 the rider will rely on.

If the judge treats locking the doors of a moving car as a dangerous-driving / confinement allegation, the case goes to a person under SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 regardless of the driver's otherwise clean record (F8), and no automated outcome favourable to the driver is available.

points.response: Conceded in substance: the case does turn on the reading of F3 and F4, and SAFE-1 assigns that reading to a human, which is exactly why my client seeks escalation rather than an automated finding against the fare.

F6 is the driver's own post-trip statement and the policy treats a driver's assertion as a claim, not a system record; the only system-anchored account of the exchange is the verbatim chat F3 then F4 one minute later (F5), which shows the rider's request was met with a lock-the-doors conditional.
I do not contest the route: F1 shows 15.4 km versus 15.5 km optimal, so RD-1/RD-2 add nothing here and my client makes no detour claim.
I do not claim a distance-based overcharge; the $32.86 is a fixed quote (F1), and my escalation rests on the safety reading of F4, not on FARE-1 or RD-2.

A clean 90-day record (F8) is irrelevant to whether F4 reads as intimidation - profile facts may support a flag_account request but can never decide the case - and it is no answer to the 22 minutes between F3 (17:09) and drop-off (F2) during which the rider had asked to get out.

Conceded in part: F4's words are the hinge of this case, so I do not ask the judge to read them as a threat, I ask only that SAFE-1's own test be applied — whether the words constitute 'threat, intimidation' is to be read from the words and their context, and here the words sit one minute after F3 in a moving vehicle where the rider had reached for the door, so the reading is genuinely contested and belongs to a person.

Accepted only as to the sequence: F5 confirms two timestamped messages F3 (17:09) and F4 (17:10) and I do not dispute that order; but F5 establishes timing, not meaning, and it says nothing that makes F6's account of why the words were said false, so it cannot do the work of proving a threat.

F6 is a driver statement, not a system record, and it is misread as an admission — it records a safety instruction ('I told her to sit down for her own safety') after the rider reached for the door at lights, and 'drove on' describes continuing the trip to the named destination, not confinement; no system fact (F1, F2) shows the trip ever left the optimal route or stopped unexpectedly.

I do not contest that the $32.86 fixed RydeX fare is untainted by any route or billing defect — F1 shows 15.4 km against 15.5 km optimal (-0.1 km, -0%) and F2 only 1.9 min over estimate — so no RD-2 or FARE-1 amount exists for the rider to recover on the fare side.

Escalation is the outcome I myself seek, so this claim is not contested; I ask only that the file handed to the human reviewer include F1, F2 and F6 alongside F3 and F4, since the record shows a driver with 1038 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F8) whose GPS track is shorter than optimal.
